newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli, PLO leaders talk by phone - official.
newsitem.headline: Israeli, PLO leaders talk by phone - official.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat spoke on Sunday by telephone, reviving contacts the PLO severed over Israeli policies, an adviser to Netanyahu said.

"All I can confirm is that there was a three-way telephone call from the prime minister's office with Arafat," adviser David Bar-Illan told Reuters. Jordan's King Hussein, meeting Netanyahu, was the third participant, he said.
Asked what had emerged from the more than two hours of talks, Bar-Illan said: "Just a feeling that a line of communication has been reopened."

Asked if there was an effort to get Netanyahu and Arafat together, he said: "You can say that." Asked if a meeting might be arranged on Sunday night or Monday, Bar-Illan said: "I don't have any confirmation on that.

Netanyahu then convened a news conference with King Hussein, on a visit to pay condolences to the families of seven schoolgirls slaughtered last week by a Jordanian soldier and to defuse tensions over peace moves.
